title: How Billions in Safe Insurance Money Is Being Bet on A.I. Debt
lede: The New York Times reports that US life insurers, normally among the most cautious investors, held $85.2 billion of AI-related debt by mid-year, much of it rated safe by Moody's and S&P.

points: A Musk-linked entity borrowed to buy chips and lease them to xAI, keeping the debt off xAI's books; Athene bought $2.4 billion of it.
Life insurers' AI debt holdings rose 24% in the six months to June 30, according to Moody's.
That is about 2.1% of their total debt holdings, but Moody's expects up to $185 billion by the end of next year.
Insurers such as Athene and Corebridge Financial invest money that backs life policies and retiree annuities.

points.text: Commenters split on the framing: if rating agencies call the debt safe it is not a bet, while a reply recalls AAA ratings on pre-2008 mortgage bonds.
Against talk of a new financial crisis, a reply argues the scale is far smaller and the borrowers are not critical to the economy.
Some worry the spending already drives shortages of RAM, GPUs, SSDs and now circuit boards, hurting other industries.
One commenter says the exposure reaches pension funds and private credit too, not only insurers.
